query: For a selected high-entropy alloy whose superconducting behavior remains uncharacterized, what governs whether and how superconductivity emerges in the low-temperature test regime, and why? Propose one testable mechanistic hypothesis, a controlled comparison with the starting state, the observations expected relative to that baseline, the limits over which the hypothesis should hold, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Local chemical short-range ordering (SRO) in the CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy enhances the electronic density of states at the Fermi level and electron–phonon coupling, triggering a superconducting transition below ~4 K.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy with a macroscopically single-phase, random solid solution and no detectable superconductivity above 0.3 K.
generation.intervention: Anneal the as-cast alloy at 600 °C for 24 h in vacuum to induce local chemical SRO without macroscopic phase separation.
generation.conditions: Measure resistivity and AC susceptibility from 0.3 K to 10 K in zero applied magnetic field on both as-cast and annealed specimens, under identical cooling protocols.
generation.structural_mediator: Degree of chemical short-range order quantified by the Warren–Cowley SRO parameter extracted from atomic pair distribution function (PDF) or high-energy X-ray diffuse scattering.
generation.mechanism: Annealing-induced SRO clusters enrich elements with strong electron–phonon coupling (e.g. Ni, Co) in nanometer regions, raising the local density of states N(EF) and coupling constant λ enough to exceed the threshold for superconductivity.
generation.predicted_outcome: The annealed alloy will exhibit a clear superconducting transition (onset T_c ≈ 2–4 K, zero resistivity and diamagnetic response) corresponding to a superconducting volume fraction >50%, whereas the as-cast alloy remains normal down to 0.3 K.
generation.baseline: As-cast CrMnFeCoNi shows no superconductivity above 0.3 K and a low N(EF) (~1 state/eV-atom) consistent with weak electron–phonon coupling.
generation.boundary: Holds for SRO fractions up to ~20% induced by annealing at 500–700 °C for 12–48 h; excessive ordering (beyond ~25% SRO) or formation of second phases should disrupt percolating superconducting regions and suppress Tc.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate uncertainty in the exact T_c and required SRO fraction, due to absence of prior SRO–superconductivity correlation data in this specific alloy system.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two CrMnFeCoNi specimens: (a) as-cast and (b) annealed at 600 °C/24 h. Characterize SRO via PDF/diffuse scattering and measure resistivity and AC susceptibility down to 0.3 K.
measurements: Warren–Cowley SRO parameter from PDF or diffuse scattering
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the annealed specimen shows no superconducting transition above 0.3 K despite a measurable increase in SRO, or if T_c does not correlate positively with SRO across samples annealed for different times, the hypothesis is falsified.
